newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND TAKES WORLD CUP LEAD WITH SUPER-G WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND TAKES WORLD CUP LEAD WITH SUPER-G WIN.

text.p: Luc Alphand dismissed his disappointing world Alpine skiing championships as "water under the bridge" after taking the lead in the World Cup with a super-G triumph on Friday.

The Frenchman, who crashed out of the downhill at this month's championships in Sestriere and finished only 12th in the super-G, showed control and composure on one of the most challenging courses in the sport to take the lead in the overall standings.

"Forget about the world championships. That's all water under the bridge. I'm not thinking about them any more," said the 31-year-old downhiller who is bidding to become the first Frenchman to win the prestigious overall title since Jean-Claude Killy in 1968.
"That was one of the fastest super-Gs I have ever raced. The course was cut up and covered in ruts. It was a wild run...(but) the World Cup has given me momentum again."

With bright sunshine and warm temperatures in the relatively low German resort, the start of the race was brought forward by 90 minutes to mid-morning. There were some surprising performances from some of the later racers.

Wearing bib number three, Alphand sped down the mountain to win in one minute 15.32 seconds. Austrian Hermann Maier pulled off a shock by taking second place from start number 32 in 1:15.87, 0.55 seconds behind.

Italy's Werner Perathoner, who has just come back from knee surgery, also caused a surprise by taking third place in 1:15.90. Canada's Ed Podivinsky took fourth place in 1:15.96 after starting back in 35th.

"It was too fast for the technicians," said Alphand who replaced Kjetil Andre Aamodt at the top of the overall standings. The Norwegian finished fifth in 1:15.97 and is now 51 points behind the Frenchman overall.
With 10 races remaining, Alphand, who excels in the speed events, is still playing down his chances of beating all-rounder Aamodt to the title. There are six speeds event remaining.
The Frenchman's main goal is to win the downhill title for the third consecutive season. If he can repeat last year's triumph here in Saturday's downhill he will move a step closer to that goal.
"Aamodt is still the overall favourite as far as I'm concerned. He can ski in all the events," said Alphand who had bad memories of a crash in Garmisch in 1992 before last season's win.
"If you think about the points you get too afraid to attack. The overall World Cup is the greatest achievement. For me it is just a dream. I don't like to think about it."
The result marked only the second super-G victory of Alphand's career after his triumph in the Swiss resort of Laax last month.
Norway's Atle Skaardal, the world champion in Sestriere, made a mistake at the top of the course when he lost control of one of his skis and he finished only 10th in 1:16.22.
Maier broke his arm earlier in the season but has shown good form in recent training and was not surprised by his second place despite his high start number.
Perathoner's third place with start number 11 was even more remarkable as he had surgery on his left knee at the start of the month and was unable to compete in Sestriere.
